We want this site to work for everyone. It aims to meet the Web Content
Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) 2.1 at level AA: text has enough contrast,
everything works by keyboard, and images have text alternatives.

The homepage is laid out like a coding notebook. Each cell's output appears
when you scroll to it or press the cell's run button. All of the text is in
the page from the start, so screen readers and search engines get all of it.

- **Keyboard.** Tab to a cell, then press Shift+Enter to run it and move to
  the next one, or Ctrl+Enter (⌘+Enter on a Mac) to run it in place.
- **Screen readers.** When a cell runs, the first line of its output is read
  out. The globe animation has a text description.
- **Motion.** The globe animation has a Pause button. If your device asks for
  reduced motion, the site turns its animations off: the homepage shows every
  output at once, the headline appears without typing itself, and the globes
  hold still.

If you meet a barrier on this site, or need a document in another format,
please tell us. We will do our best to help.
